channel.title: Pier & Point · SF Railyards
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for SF Railyards (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · SF Railyards: SF Railyards now uses real Assessor lot lines.
item.description: SF Railyards now uses real Assessor lot lines. Source: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001.

item.title: Correction · SF Railyards: The record and an earlier timeline entry had said roughly 2,500 homes and up to 4 million square feet of commercial space; the SF Standard (March 10, 2026) says up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total, half commercial, with an 850-foot tower, and the January 2025 Chronicle article is now dated correctly. The 2022 outreach start is given as a year (the FAQ says fall 2022). The map notes now say DataSF has King St centerline segments from 6th to 7th St and that three active Assessor parcels lie inside the mapped area, correcting two earlier statements, and the inference that the site lies outside Mission Bay North was removed because DataSF's project-area layer puts about 41% of it inside 'Mission Bay - North'. The Board of Supervisors entry no longer names a district or supervisor.

item.title: Added · SF Railyards: New adjacent record: the SF Railyards, a 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and the 4th & King Street Station, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual operating easement, adjoining Mission Bay North. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP, per the January 2025 Planning Commission packet); Prologis has floated a concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), with an 850-foot tower (SF Standard, March 10, 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path (SF Planning FAQ). The map shape is bounded by real street centerlines (Townsend, 4th, 7th, King), not a surveyed parcel; see the record's accuracy note. Pier & Point records the process and does not take a position.
